# Pending changes (since patch 0025, 2026-11-26)
- (2026-11-26, a cut picked from its ghost) Asked: the negative solid (a cut) can't be selected or seen in the
  overview. A live boolean's tool solid has no part of its own - it lives in the solid's recipe and shows as a
  ghost. Now a click on a tool step's ghost (cut / join / common)
  picks that step - its solid selected, its ghost turned the picked colour - and a drag moves the step whole
  (its placement in the recipe, b_xf - a revolved cut keeps its shape; moving its profile curve reshaped it
  instead), one undo step; right-click calls it off (_step_to, _step_word)
  (CurveTools._ghost_hit, _ray_mesh, pick_step; ghosts remember their solid and step - a ghost is drawn
  over everything, so one seen under the mouse wins the click over a solid in front of it). The overview lists a
  solid's tool steps even with the solid folded (_tree_step_rows). Tests: test_cut_picked_from_its_ghost.
  Files: scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd, tests/test_curve_modeling.gd.
- (2026-11-26, a moved cut updates its solid and its edge) Reported: moving the negative didn't update the
  solid it cuts, and its edge stayed where it was until clicked away. The cut - a revolved arc whose ends
  sat 0.2 mm off the axis (left so by an earlier drag of its edge) - had pinholes at its poles, and a
  boolean needs a closed solid: it failed silently and the solid kept its old mesh. Revolves now put a
  profile's ends within a thousandth of its size of the axis onto it (closed poles). The edge lines' change
  check counted the edges' placements, not what they are: now hashed, so a moved step's edges are drawn
  where it went at once. Tests: test_revolve_near_axis_is_closed_and_cuts, test_lines_follow_a_moved_step.
  Files: scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd, tests/test_curve_modeling.gd.
- (2026-11-26, Simplify keeps the shape) Reported: simplifying an edge didn't keep its shape and messed up the
  topology. Simplify flattened the edge onto the plane of its stored normal (a rim round a curved solid
  isn't flat), and changed a baked solid's edge's points without placing its edge points along it again.
  Now it works in 3D: the vertices that matter kept (Douglas-Peucker, loose first, finer till the result -
  a smooth path, corners sharp - keeps within half a percent of the edge's size; the user's rims 41 -> 8
  and 43 -> 16 vertices, ~3 mm off on a 1.4 m solid); a baked solid's mesh is kept as it is, its edge
  points on that edge placed along it anew (_reparam_holding). Tests: test_simplify_keeps_a_curved_rim.
  Files: scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd, tests/test_curve_modeling.gd.
- (2026-11-26, baking a boolean without slivers) Reported: baking made messy topology, too many triangles
  instead of quads. A boolean's cut through a curved solid (a revolved sphere cut by another) left the even
  remesh full of slivers: 5,142 triangles, 1,903 of them thin. Baking now, when over 5% of its triangles
  are thin, merges points too close together and makes the triangles even inside each face, shape kept
  (EdgeNet.tidy_mesh, even_faces) - they then pair into quads: 3,782 triangles, 15 thin before pairing,
  volume within 0.1%. The user's baked sphere cleaned the same way (one undo step; backed up first).
  Tests: test_baked_cut_sphere_has_few_slivers.
  Files: scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd, tests/test_curve_modeling.gd.
- (2026-11-26, quads that follow the edges - begun) Asked: every operation, baking included, makes quad-based
  topology with a uniform layout, the quads following the flow and shape of the edges - the main rules for
  any topology (now in CLAUDE.md). Splitting triangles into quads (quadify) doesn't follow anything, so baking
  got EdgeNet.grid_faces: each edge (between where edges meet) sampled evenly once - the faces either side
  share its points; each face's four corners (its sharpest; opposite sides' counts balanced) and a harmonic
  map onto a square (conjugate gradients); a grid of quads laid there and mapped back - rows along its
  edges. It's used when every face of the bake can be one even grid (enough quads for its size, none over
  4x the mean); otherwise baking keeps the even mesh (slivers cleared, triangles paired into quads) and
  EdgeNet.grid_why says why. Not yet: faces that can't be one grid - a dome round a small rim (the user's
  cut sphere), faces with more than four corners (a notched face) - need splitting into several four-sided
  patches; next. Files: scripts/editor/mesh/edge_net.gd (grid_faces, _face_grid), scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd
  (bake), CLAUDE.md, tests/test_curve_modeling.gd.
- (2026-11-26, quads that follow the edges - every face) Asked: yes - faces that can't be one grid made of
  patches too. EdgeNet.grid_faces now lays every face out: four balanced corners - one grid (_face_grid);
  any other face - a dome round a small rim, a face of many corners - rings of quads following its boundary
  inwards round a middle grid (_face_rings: the face mapped onto a disc, evened out by area, the rings placed
  at equal lengths along each spoke and the middle grid sized on the surface - the quads about the boundary's
  spacing either way); a ring-shaped face (two loops - a cut through a solid's side, a tunnel) - rows running
  from one loop to the other, both loops given the same count and paired without a twist (_face_annulus).
  Quads face as the surface under each does (_quads_out). Baking uses it for every bake that isn't rows of
  quads already (dense 3: its settles keep the quads). The user's cut sphere: 3,782 triangles in no order ->
  1,280 in quads along its rims (backed up first, one undo step); the test sphere: 2,684 -> 2,508, stretched
  quads 37% -> 8%. Tests: test_bake_lays_quads_along_the_edges, test_baked_dome_rings_follow_its_rim,
  test_baked_tunnel_rows_run_between_its_rims. Still to improve: a crease where a dome's rings meet its middle
  grid; the grid's points lie on the even mesh it's mapped from (a slightly faceted surface); bakes of this
  kind take 0.5-1.3 s on the main thread.
- (2026-11-26, the settings panel inside the window) Reported: the settings dialog oversize, not kept within
  the window's edges. Its Controls page laid its five key groups side by side in one row (~2,960 px at the
  current text size) and the settings scroll took that width - a 3,043 px panel in a 1,920 px window. The
  groups now flow onto a new line when they don't fit (HFlowContainer), and the panel's width is never more
  than the window's less a margin (MainMenu._fit) - 1,864 px there. A menu built before the change turns its
  row of columns into the flow itself (self-healing - live; the page it looks in is the one built inside
  the tab's page, both named ControlsPage). The scroll's height is fitted again once the wrapped groups are
  laid out (their height comes with their width). File: scripts/ui/main_menu.gd.
- (2026-11-26, the Controls page laid out cleanly) Asked: some text cut or with no space before its buttons;
  align the buttons, two or more lines for long text; every tab the same height. The Controls page fits its
  text (MainMenu._fit_controls, again when bindings or the text size change): every binding button and its
  KEY / ALT KEY / GAMEPAD heading as wide as the longest binding shown (its style's margins counted - "D-pad
  down" was cut), one name width for every column (about fifteen letters, a gap before the buttons) so the
  buttons line up down the page, longer names wrapping onto more lines with their buttons centred beside
  them. "Trade routes on the maps" moved up with the other Menus actions (Keybinds.ACTIONS) - it had made a
  second Menus column; an open menu folds such a split group back itself. Every settings tab now the height
  of the tallest (within the window). Files: scripts/ui/main_menu.gd, scripts/core/keybinds.gd.
- (2026-11-26, a middle click resets the zoom) Asked: in the game, clicking the middle mouse button resets
  the zoom the wheel controls. CosmosCam: a middle click puts the wheel's zoom back where it started - flying
  (1.35), on foot (1.0), in a passenger seat the ship's own start (Cosmos.passenger_view notes it); not while
  the builder is out on foot (the middle button turns its piece). In flight it still centres the stick too.
  The guide says so. Tests: test_cosmos.test_middle_click_resets_the_zoom. Files:
  scripts/world/player/cosmos_cam.gd, scripts/world/space/cosmos.gd, data/docs/game.md, tests/test_cosmos.gd.
- (2026-11-26, fullscreen at a chosen resolution) Asked: fullscreen should let the resolution be set in the
  settings, not just use the screen's. The screen keeps its own mode (the engine can't switch it), but the
  world is drawn at the resolution picked and scaled up to fill it (the root viewport's 3D scale - the menus
  and the HUD stay sharp at the screen's size); windowed it's the window's size as before. The resolution
  list stays enabled in fullscreen and offers the screen's own size too; its tooltips say what it does.
  Tests: test_display. Files: scripts/core/settings.gd (render_scale, _apply_render_scale,
  available_resolutions), scripts/ui/main_menu.gd, tests/test_display.gd. (Also: the guide's 3D shots taken
  again - their scripts changed.)
- (2026-11-26, the resolution everywhere; fullscreen kept true; a settings panel its own size) Reported:
  leaving fullscreen didn't show in the settings; the resolution applied to the world but not the menus -
  make it the same everywhere; the settings panel oversized. Fullscreen at a resolution under the screen's
  now draws everything - the world, the menus, the HUD - at that resolution, laid out as ever (1920 x 1080),
  scaled up to fill the screen (Settings.frame_plan: the root window's viewport stretch at that size, its 2D
  scale keeping the layout); otherwise the usual stretch (replaces drawing only the 3D smaller). The window
  watched: left or entered fullscreen some other way (the window manager's keys), the setting follows, is
  saved, and the settings page's switch shows it (Settings._window_changed, display_changed). The settings
  panel is now as wide as the widest of its pages with the key groups one under another (1,020 px at the
  user's text size, was the whole window) and every tab its height, the Controls page's worked out before
  it's been laid out. Files: scripts/core/settings.gd, scripts/ui/main_menu.gd, tests/test_display.gd.
- (2026-11-26, a window draws at its own size) Reported: back in a window from fullscreen, the game still drew
  at 4K into its 1080p window. Settings set the mode and the window's size on the display server, behind the
  game's own window: the window shrank, the game's root window kept the screen's size and drew its frames at
  it. Now through the root Window (its mode, size, position); and whenever the window resizes, a windowed
  root whose size differs from the window's real one is put right. Checked in a window on a 3840 x 2160
  screen: fullscreen at 1080p drawn at 1920 x 1080 and scaled up; back in a 1280 x 720 window, drawn at
  1280 x 720. File: scripts/core/settings.gd.
- (2026-11-27, out of fullscreen at once; the window watched; the Esc menu too) Reported: the settings dialog
  took too long to come back after leaving fullscreen - should be instant; test the Esc menu too. Timed in a
  window on a 4K screen: leaving fullscreen from the settings was a 0.68 s frame. Two causes: switching the
  stretch mode (every text laid out again) - now one way always: the frame drawn at the resolution picked,
  windowed or fullscreen (Settings.frame_plan: [drawing size, 2D scale]), so in and out changes only the
  window; and resizing the window straight after leaving fullscreen, while the window manager was still
  putting it back (0.75 s) - now left to come back by itself, sized after only if it isn't the resolution
  picked. Out of fullscreen now ~0.1 s (the window manager's own), title and the in-game Esc menu alike; the
  dialog keeps its size and place. Drawing at a fixed size, the game hears no resize when only the window
  changes, so Settings looks at the window four times a second: fullscreen entered or left with the window
  manager's keys - the setting follows, is saved, and the settings' switch shows it (checked in the Esc
  menu). No window in a headless run: display settings left alone there (a test's editor view had taken
  the window's 1920 x 1080 and its picks moved). Files: scripts/core/settings.gd, scripts/ui/main_menu.gd,
  tests/test_display.gd.
